concepts.name: Variation in reproduction
concepts.description: Each generation inherits a common body design with small changes; asexual reproduction creates only minor differences from DNA-copying errors, sexual reproduction creates more, and environmental selection of variants underlies evolution.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §8.1, p.128-129 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Inheritance from both parents
concepts.description: Father and mother contribute about equal genetic material, so every trait can be influenced by paternal and maternal DNA and each child carries two versions of each trait.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §8.2.2, p.129 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Dominant and recessive traits
concepts.description: When the two copies of a factor differ, the one that is expressed is dominant and the hidden one is recessive (TT and Tt plants are tall; only tt plants are short).
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §8.2.2, p.130 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Mendel's monohybrid cross
concepts.description: Mendel's tall x short pea cross: all F1 plants are tall, and when they self-pollinate a quarter of the F2 are short (TT:Tt:tt = 1:2:1), which led him to propose two copies of each factor.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §8.2.2, p.130 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Independent inheritance of traits
concepts.description: In a cross involving two traits (seed shape and colour, or height and seed shape), the traits are inherited independently, so new combinations appear in the F2 (about 9:3:3:1).
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §8.2.2, p.131 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Genes and how traits are expressed
concepts.description: A gene is a section of DNA that carries information for one protein; proteins such as enzymes control traits, e.g. an enzyme's efficiency sets how much growth hormone is made and so how tall a plant grows.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §8.2.3, p.131 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Chromosomes and germ cells
concepts.description: Body cells have two gene sets, as separate pieces called chromosomes, one copy of each from each parent; germ cells take one chromosome from every pair, and fertilisation restores the normal number.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §8.2.3, p.131-132 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Sex determination
concepts.description: Some species use environmental cues (temperature in some reptiles) or can change sex (snails); in humans sex is largely genetic: women are XX, men XY, and the father's X or Y decides the child's sex.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §8.2.4, p.132 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)
